name: Bordering countries
region_note: region is null: Canada and Mexico are not US regions, and 'territories' would be wrong. npdes_authority 'mixed' is a placeholder: no US NPDES authority applies outside the US (Canada: provincial approvals plus the federal WSER; Mexico: CONAGUA discharge permits under NOM-001-SEMARNAT).

law.summary: Canada: operators report to provinces (Ontario Spills Action Centre and medical officer of health under CLI-ECAs; Quebec SOMAEU under ROMAEU) and to ECCC annually under WSER; public real-time notice is not a general duty, but Kingston, Windsor and Metro Vancouver publish voluntarily. Mexico: no public notice duty known; binational IBWC protocols require CESPT and OOMAPAS to tell the Mexican Section, which tells USIBWC, which emails a US list and files reports with the San Diego Water Board.

citations.cite: Binational Tijuana River Spill Notification Protocol (IBWC)
citations.title: Initial Binational Tijuana River Spill Notification Protocol
citations.quote: In the event of occurrence of the events described in points No. 1 or No. 3 above, USIBWC will immediately notify U.S. recipients of USIBWC email list serve developed for these cases.
citations.who: USIBWC (after CESPT and the Mexican Section)
citations.channel: email list; spill report to San Diego Water Board and Cal OES
citations.deadline: CESPT to Mexican Section 'within the hour, whenever this is possible'; USIBWC 'immediately'
citations.threshold: pump or pipeline failure that can result in raw sewage reaching the boundary

citations.cite: Order No. R9-2021-0001 as amended (NPDES CA0108928)
citations.title: USIBWC South Bay IWTP permit, spill and transboundary flow reporting
citations.quote: submits preliminary Spill Event and dry weather Canyon Collector Transboundary Flow Event reports within three days of the event and submits monthly reports on river flows
citations.channel: San Diego Water Board, posted as a public table
citations.threshold: spill events and dry-weather transboundary flows

citations.title: Sewage collection system reporting

waters.hydrography_note: NHD and NLDI stop at the border. North: NRCan National Hydro Network / Canadian Hydrospatial Network (OGL-Canada); south: INEGI Red Hidrográfica; OpenStreetMap waterways for names on both. For waters flowing into the US the downstream reach starts at the boundary crossing, where NHD takes over.

readiness.rationale: Shared waters next to live states (Lake Champlain and Memphremagog for VT/NY, Lake Ontario and the Niagara for NY, the St. Croix for ME) have only annual or monthly foreign data, except Windsor's bypass CSV (Detroit River, MI not live) and Kingston's map (bot wall). The best dated source, the Tijuana table, is beside California, which is not live. Start with Quebec's outfall points and monthly summaries for the Vermont waters.

owner_questions: Show foreign monthly or annual totals (Quebec, WSER) on US water pages as 'monthly' or 'annual' marks, attributed to the foreign authority?
Treat the Tijuana River's ongoing transboundary flow (listed as one event since 2023-10-11) as a standing condition rather than an event?
Ask Utilities Kingston for data access, and join the USIBWC spill list?
Use the OpenStreetMap or NRCan networks north of the border, or stop at the boundary and attach foreign outfalls to the first US reach?
surprise: The richest cross-border event record is a California Water Board HTML table of Mexican spills, while Canada's best real-time overflow map (Kingston, on Lake Ontario beside New York) is behind a bot wall, and the Richelieu, the obvious Lake Champlain candidate, flows away from the US entirely.
